current_work: Investigating calibration robustness to noisy target prevalence estimates
Comparing calibration methods under controlled prevalence perturbations
Maintaining research code and experiment infrastructure
Preparing a focused pilot analysis for a potential follow-up study
priorities: Determine whether the observed method-by-noise interaction is reproducible
Keep the pilot analysis bounded and methodologically consistent
Document the evidence well enough to support a decision about broader experiments
Avoid expanding the study before the current question is resolved

circumstances: The researcher reviews the stopping criteria from Day 27 and decides that one confirmation seed is justified because the class-level reversal could materially change the interpretation. The confirmation run uses the same dataset, methods, noise levels, and standardized metrics. The overall interaction is directionally similar, but the class-level reversal is weaker and no longer clearly separated from uncertainty. The researcher checks whether the apparent interaction changes when the lowest-frequency class is excluded and finds that the aggregate pattern becomes smoother. They document the result as suggestive rather than definitive and begin outlining a small methods note. Later, they briefly investigate a GitHub implementation detail and unrelated laptop storage information before returning to the research question.

activities.title: Run the pre-specified confirmation comparison
activities.summary: The researcher reviewed the stopping criteria, validated the unchanged configuration and dataset, and ran one confirmation seed using the same methods, noise levels, and standardized metrics.
activities.context: A confirmation run was justified by the possibility that the class-level reversal could materially affect interpretation.

activities.title: Analyze confirmation results and test class-level sensitivity
activities.summary: The confirmation run was directionally similar overall, but the class-level reversal was weaker and overlapped uncertainty. Excluding the lowest-frequency class made the aggregate pattern smoother, suggesting that the earlier reversal was sensitive to class composition.
activities.context: Testing whether the surprising Day 27 result was robust enough to support a broader claim.

activities.title: Document the pilot interpretation
activities.summary: The researcher outlined a concise methods note and documented the confirmation result, evaluation protocol, and limitations, reducing confidence in the class-level reversal.
activities.context: Capturing the current evidence before deciding whether the pilot warrants expansion.

activities.title: Brief implementation check and unrelated browsing
activities.summary: The researcher checked implementation details in a related calibration repository, then spent a short period looking up laptop storage information unrelated to the research question.

activities.title: Narrow the research question and close the pilot expansion loop
activities.summary: The researcher revised the methods note and research question to describe the method-by-noise interaction as suggestive rather than definitive, and decided to keep the dataset fixed rather than expanding the study immediately.
activities.context: Decision after the confirmation run weakened the strongest interpretation of the initial result.

key_observations: The confirmation run broadly preserves the direction of the method-by-noise interaction, but the class-level reversal seen previously is weaker and not clearly separated from uncertainty.
Removing the lowest-frequency class makes the aggregate pattern smoother, suggesting that part of the earlier irregularity may depend on class composition.
The evidence is currently better described as suggestive method sensitivity than as a stable ranking or method-specific failure.
A concise methods note now records the standardized protocol and limitations, making the pilot easier to evaluate without immediately expanding the experiment matrix.
The researcher explicitly decided to keep the dataset fixed for now.
priority_alignment: The planned confirmation run was completed using the existing configuration.
The analysis tested a plausible source of instability without adding another dataset.
The research question was narrowed in response to weaker evidence rather than expanded to preserve an interesting result.
important_uncertainty: It remains unclear whether the method-by-noise interaction is reproducible beyond the two confirmation seeds.
The apparent low-frequency-class effect may be dataset-specific.
The current evidence is not strong enough to support a broad claim about calibration methods under prevalence-estimation noise.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Review the two-seed pilot and decide whether it is sufficient for a bounded methods note or whether one additional pre-specified seed is warranted; do not add another dataset yet.

primary_action.title: Decide the pilot stopping point
primary_action.reason: The confirmation run weakened the strongest interpretation, so the next useful action is to decide whether the current evidence is enough for a bounded note rather than automatically adding more experiments.

secondary_action.title: Finish the methods note
secondary_action.reason: The standardized protocol and limitations are already documented; consolidating them will preserve the result even if the pilot is stopped.

things_not_to_do: Do not add a second dataset simply because the class-level effect weakened.
Do not describe the confirmation result as proof of a stable method ranking.
Do not keep searching for implementations or papers until a preferred interpretation appears.
Do not turn the laptop-storage browsing into a recurring research interruption.
